4_sql_level_numbers_reproduce_exactly.claim: current predicate = 1294 reads / 100-155ms CPU (16588 matches); dropping LOWER() = identical 1294 reads / 80-92ms CPU / same 16588 matches; prefix LIKE 'the%' = 1294 reads / 12-13ms but only 3859 matches; no-q count = 133 reads
4_sql_level_numbers_reproduce_exactly.method: SET STATISTICS IO/TIME ON, python sweep/v8/sqlrun.py
4_sql_level_numbers_reproduce_exactly.verdict: CONFIRMED on all four points. Match counts (16588, 3859, 43735) and logical reads (1294, 1294, 1294, 133) match the claim exactly. Dropping LOWER() keeps the SAME match count and the SAME reads (plan unchanged, no index available) — exactly as claimed. My CPU milliseconds run somewhat higher than the claim's (machine load differs) but the ordering and ratios hold.
4_sql_level_numbers_reproduce_exactly.honest_caveat: The claim's '100-155ms CPU for current vs 80-92ms for no-LOWER' was not reproducible to the millisecond here (I measured 108-155 vs 106-196 with the JOIN; and 184 vs 184 with NO JOIN, i.e. on the bare table the LOWER() saving is ~0). The direction ('LOWER() costs some CPU, does not change the plan') is right; the exact 20ms delta is machine-dependent and is not the load-bearing part of the claim — the load-bearing part (full scan, no index, leading wildcard) reproduces perfectly.

5_where_the_185ms_actually_goes.method: delta of sys.dm_exec_query_stats around one live call to the endpoint

measured.q=zygomorphic (0 matches): count 1301 reads / 28822us CPU; page 4724 reads / 171039us CPU / 40755us elapsed
measured.no-q: count 1301 reads / 28822us CPU; page 4724 reads / 171039us CPU

5_where_the_185ms_actually_goes.finding: With q, the COUNT's CPU jumps from ~29ms (no-q) to ~116ms — that delta is the non-sargable LIKE over all 43735 rows. The page statement's CPU is essentially q-independent (~127-171ms) because its catch-all `(:lessonId IS NULL OR ...)` predicate scans regardless. So the claim correctly attributes the +~60ms of API latency to the LIKE count, but the endpoint would not be fast even with a perfect search index: the page statement carries its own full scan.

7_is_it_a_bug_or_correct_behaviour.endpoint_is_admin_only: AdminExerciseController:27 @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')"); live control: student token -> HTTP 403 on the same URL. Confirmed admin-only.
7_is_it_a_bug_or_correct_behaviour.the_claim_does_not_assert_a_bug: The claim explicitly concludes 'Verdict: do not optimize' and classifies the real wins (prefix search, SQL Server full-text) as PRODUCT decisions that change search semantics (q=the would stop matching 'theory'). It is a documented refusal-to-act, not a defect report.
7_is_it_a_bug_or_correct_behaviour.source_is_intentional: ExerciseRepository.findAdminPage uses LOWER(...) LIKE LOWER(CONCAT('%',:keyword,'%')) on question and explanation — deliberately a contains-search over both fields, shared by the admin screen. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS is already case-insensitive, which is why dropping LOWER() changes nothing.
7_is_it_a_bug_or_correct_behaviour.verdict: The behaviour is correct/intended. This is a performance characteristic with an explicit, evidence-backed decision not to optimize, not a bug.

severity_note: Claimed LOW. The measurement is real and is the slowest endpoint in the app's 35-endpoint sweep, so LOW is defensible. Strictly, because the claim is by its own terms a non-actionable, admin-only observation whose conclusion is 'do not optimize', the correct disposition is INFORMATIONAL rather than an actionable LOW defect. This is a framing correction only — it does not undermine the evidence.
why_not_refuted: Every load-bearing number reproduces: 185.1ms -> 183.1ms (my interleaved median); 16588 / 3859 / 43735 match counts exact; 1294 / 1294 / 1294 / 133 logical reads exact; 6 indexes none on question; plan = Clustered Index Scan on PK + lower() filter.
The root cause is proven, not speculated: the plan was pulled from a real ShowPlanXML, not inferred.
No probe artefact: no 429, and the number survives a re-measurement on a quiet stack (removing the one weakness the original artifact itself flagged — concurrent sweep + backend restarts).
The claim does not overreach: it recommends NO code change, so there is no fix to dispute.
residual_issues_in_the_claim_worth_recor: The claim's CPU ms (100-155 current / 80-92 no-LOWER) did not reproduce to the millisecond; on the bare table (no JOIN) LOWER() costs ~0 CPU. The 20ms 'saving' is machine-dependent and is not what justifies the decision — the missing index and non-sargable leading wildcard are.

The claim's 'prefix LIKE the% = 3859 matches' is the question-only prefix count; the actual endpoint ORs explanation too, so the semantically-correct prefix count is 4572. The claim's point (prefix changes semantics / drops matches) stands either way.

The endpoint would still scan ~4-5k logical reads on the page statement even with an ideal question index, because the page query's catch-all predicate is separately non-sargable. The claim attributes the whole endpoint cost to the LIKE; it is ~half right (the count half).
side_effects: All probes were GET-only plus login POSTs. No rows created or deleted. PROBE_LEFT=0. No source code modified.
